subject: Next steps — scheduling a 30‑min product briefing (stakeholder pairings)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Hannah Lee <hannah.lee@orchardtech.com>, Michael Ortega <m.ortega@orchardtech.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps — scheduling a 30‑min product briefing (stakeholder pairings)

Hi Hannah / Michael —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we’re aligned before we schedule the next session: 

- Primary goals: reduce inference latency on user-facing features by ~40% and cut per‑token cost for high‑volume endpoints.
- Key constraints: strict data residency requirements for logs, SSO via Okta, and a desire to keep a predictable monthly spend.
- Top stakeholders to include for the next call: one PM (product/roadmap), one engineering lead (infra/MLops), and optionally a C‑level exec for procurement alignment.

Suggested next step: a focused 30‑minute product briefing where we demo the runtime, show latency/cost tradeoffs, and sketch a mutual action plan. To make scheduling easy, propose two stakeholder pairings (pick the one that maps to who will join):

Option A — Product + Engineering (shorter technical demo + big‑picture roadmap)
- Tues, 11/09 — 10:00–10:30 PT
- Ideal attendees: Product manager, Engineering lead

Option B — Engineering + Exec (tech deep dive + procurement touchpoints)
- Wed, 11/10 — 14:00–14:30 PT
- Ideal attendees: Engineering lead, CTO/Head of Eng

Option C — Two windows if you need morning vs afternoon flexibility
- Thurs, 11/11 — 09:00–09:30 PT OR 16:00–16:30 PT

Please reply with the option that works best and confirm who will join (names + roles). I’ve attached a short mutual action plan (MAP_OrchardTech_v1.pdf) and I can send an agenda + calendar invite once we lock the time.

If you’d like any specific metrics/demo scenarios covered (e.g., 512 tokens @ p95 latency, or multi‑tenant routing examples), tell me and I’ll make sure Vivek covers those.

Thanks — look forward to getting something on the calendar.

—
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555‑0189
Redwood Inference

Attachments: MAP_OrchardTech_v1.pdf (1 page, mutual action plan stub)

From: Hannah Lee <hannah.lee@orchardtech.com>

Cc: Michael Ortega <m.ortega@orchardtech.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 17:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps — scheduling a 30‑min product briefing (stakeholder pairings)

Thanks Neha — useful recap. Option B (Wed 11/10 14:00 PT) works best for our timeline.

Two quick notes: 
1) Can you include our CTO Lauren Park (lauren.park@orchardtech.com)? She’d like to join this one.
2) Please send a brief agenda so we can make sure procurement and platform folks are ready.

Attendees from our side: 
- Hannah Lee — Product (you know me)
- Michael Ortega — Engineering (infra lead)
- Lauren Park — CTO (confirming)

If you need to swap to Option A we'll follow up, but let’s try Option B first.

Subject: Re: Next steps — scheduling a 30‑min product briefing (stakeholder pairings)

Perfect — thanks Hannah, and welcome Lauren. I’ve locked Wed 11/10, 14:00–14:30 PT for Option B and attached a short 30‑minute agenda. The calendar invite (orchardtech-briefing-invite.ics) will go out from my calendar shortly.

Proposed 30‑minute agenda (high level):
- 0–5m: intros & success criteria (Neha + Hannah)
- 5–18m: live demo focused on latency and routing (Vivek)
- 18–25m: mutual action plan & deployment options (Neha)
- 25–30m: next steps / Q&A (all)

Pre‑read (optional): short note on our prefix/KV caching approach — link below. If Lauren wants a deeper technical appendix I can have Vivek prep an addendum.

I’ve attached: 30min-brief-agenda.pdf and orchardtech-briefing-invite.ics. Let me know if Lauren or Michael want to shift the time by +/- 30m otherwise we’ll send the invite.

—
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555‑0189
Redwood Inference

Quick note from the SE side — I’ll run the demo portion and plan to cover:
- end‑to‑end p95 latency for a 512 token prompt (baseline vs. Redwood configuration)
- batching and KV prefix caching behavior in mixed workloads
- model variant fallbacks and routing policies that you can tune for cost vs latency

If you have any specific examples or datasets you want me to run against in the demo, drop them here (or upload to the Drive link below) and I’ll include a quick run. Pre‑read: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c-pre-read-example

Looking forward — Vivek
